hunks.baseline: Jin Family of Taiyuan.
hunks.sol: The Jin Family of Taiyuan.

hunks.baseline: As its name suggests, its headquarters were in Taiyuan. But like a conglomerate in the real world, the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s influence was not limited to a single city.
hunks.sol: As its name suggested, the family was based in Taiyuan. But like a conglomerate in the real world, its influence wasn’t limited to a single city.

hunks.baseline: The family had been established for two hundred years. It had long since expanded its sphere of influence by establishing branches in county towns scattered throughout Shanxi.
hunks.sol: The family had been established two hundred years ago and had long since expanded its sphere of influence by setting up branches in county towns throughout Shanxi.

hunks.baseline: *Scout the area near Jeongyang and return within five days.*
hunks.sol: *Scout the area around Jeongyang and return within five days.*

hunks.baseline: That was the first mission assigned to the reconnaissance squad. When they heard the order, the squad members’ reactions fell into two categories.
hunks.sol: That was the reconnaissance squad’s first mission. When the squad members heard their orders, their reactions fell into two camps.

hunks.baseline: Some, like Hyuk Mujin, were disappointed. Others, like Han Yeop, let out sighs of relief.
hunks.sol: Some, like Hyuk Mujin, were disappointed. Others, like Han Yeop, sighed with relief.

hunks.baseline: Of course, neither reaction pleased me.
hunks.sol: Neither reaction pleased me.

hunks.baseline: *Still, I’d rather have a safe mission.*
hunks.sol: *Still, a safe mission is better.*

hunks.baseline: Try running into the enemy with a bunch of guys like these. It was horrifying just to imagine. I’d be safer fighting on the front lines with people I could trust.
hunks.sol: Just imagining running into the enemy with these guys was horrifying. I’d probably be safer fighting on the front lines with people I could trust.

hunks.baseline: Suppressing a sigh, I raised my fist. It was one of the hand signals I had taught them earlier. It meant stop.
hunks.sol: Suppressing a sigh, I raised my fist. It was one of the hand signals I had taught them earlier.

hunks.baseline: Snort.
hunks.sol: Stop.
Prrr.

hunks.baseline: The eleven horses moving at a moderate pace stopped with a chorus of snorts. Hyuk Mujin, riding to my right, spoke irritably.
hunks.sol: The eleven horses, which had been moving at a steady pace, halted with a chorus of snorts. Hyuk Mujin, riding to my right, spoke irritably.

hunks.baseline: I jerked my chin toward the rear. The other squad members were breathing heavily. Riding a horse was faster than traveling on foot, but it consumed a considerable amount of stamina.
hunks.sol: I jerked my chin toward the rear. The other squad members were breathing heavily. Riding was faster than traveling on foot, but it took a considerable amount of stamina.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin’s much higher Level let him endure fairly well, but fatigue was accumulating in the others.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin’s much higher Level let him hold up fairly well, but fatigue was building in the others.

hunks.baseline: “Rest if I tell you to. That’s an order.”
hunks.sol: “When I tell you to rest, rest. That’s an order.”

hunks.baseline: Ignoring Hyuk Mujin’s crumpled face, I addressed the squad.
hunks.sol: Ignoring Hyuk Mujin’s scowl, I addressed the squad.

hunks.baseline: “Fifteen minutes of rest.”
hunks.sol: “Fifteen-minute break.”

hunks.baseline: They had fifteen minutes to rest, but the reconnaissance squad members didn’t look particularly happy. That was because I immediately pulled out a large leather backpack.
hunks.sol: They had fifteen minutes to rest, but the reconnaissance squad members didn’t look particularly happy. Probably because I immediately pulled out a large leather backpack.

hunks.baseline: I reached into the backpack and thought,
hunks.sol: I reached inside and thought,

hunks.baseline: With a clatter, three shields were summoned into the backpack.
hunks.sol: With a clatter, three shields materialized inside the backpack.

hunks.baseline: The wooden shields had been coated with iron on the surface. I had taken them from the armory before leaving the Jin Family of Taiyuan. They were light, sturdy, and perfectly usable.
hunks.sol: They were wooden shields plated with iron, taken from the armory before we left the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Light, sturdy, and perfectly usable.

hunks.baseline: The three designated reconnaissance squad members accepted the shields with faces that looked ready to die.
hunks.sol: The three squad members I called accepted the shields with stricken expressions.

hunks.baseline: Those three had been forcibly selected by me as tanks.
hunks.sol: They were the tanks I had forcibly appointed.

hunks.baseline: It was a party that would be wiped out the moment it entered a Gate, but for now, I had to be satisfied with this.
hunks.sol: It was the kind of party that would be wiped out the moment it entered a Gate, but for now, this would have to do.

hunks.baseline: Next came formation.
hunks.sol: Next came formation drills.

hunks.baseline: The three shield bearers stood at the front. Six swordsmen, from Number One Hyuk Mujin through Number Six, formed the second row. Han Yeop and I took the rear.
hunks.sol: The three shield bearers took the front. Six swordsmen, from Number One Hyuk Mujin through Number Six, formed the second row. Han Yeop and I brought up the rear.

hunks.baseline: A formation focused on watching the front.
hunks.sol: The formation prioritized threats from the front.

hunks.baseline: “Spread out. Scatter and assemble. Disperse.”
hunks.sol: “Spread out. Regroup. Disperse.”

hunks.baseline: Their faces were still full of complaints, but they now carried out the commands fairly skillfully. At this point, they were much better than F-rank Hunters who had just graduated from a Hunter training center.
hunks.sol: Their faces were still full of complaints, but they carried out the commands with a fair amount of skill now. At this point, they were much better than F-rank Hunters fresh out of a Hunter training center.

hunks.baseline: *These NPCs are better than people.*
hunks.sol: *The NPCs here are better than real people.*

hunks.baseline: The reconnaissance squad members froze.
hunks.sol: The reconnaissance squad members hesitated.

hunks.baseline: “It means exactly what it says. Retreat with all your strength.”
hunks.sol: “Exactly what it sounds like. Retreat with everything you’ve got.”

hunks.baseline: “By then, formation will be meaningless. Just run with all your strength. Don’t even look back. Scatter as much as possible.”
hunks.sol: “By that point, formation won’t matter. Just run as fast as you can. Don’t look back, and scatter as widely as possible.”

hunks.baseline: The owner of the mocking voice was, naturally, Hyuk Mujin.
hunks.sol: The mocking voice belonged, naturally, to Hyuk Mujin.

hunks.baseline: “I can’t stand this any longer. Third Young Master, is war some children’s game? If you want to make nonsense sound convincing, you should at least have read one military strategy manual before coming here.”
hunks.sol: “I can’t take this anymore. Third Young Master, do you think war is some children’s game? If you want to make your nonsense sound convincing, you should at least read a military strategy manual first.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin’s open defiance drew hesitant voices from the other reconnaissance squad members.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin’s open defiance drew hesitant murmurs from the other reconnaissance squad members.

hunks.baseline: “We aren’t government soldiers, so why are we practicing formations and being forced to carry shields…?”
hunks.sol: “We aren’t government soldiers. Why are we drilling formations and being forced to carry shields…?”

hunks.baseline: “I’ve never heard of an all-out retreat.”
hunks.sol: “I’ve never even heard of an all-out retreat.”
*See? Everyone agrees with me.*

hunks.baseline: See? Everyone thinks the same way I do. Hyuk Mujin’s smug face seemed to say exactly that.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin’s smug expression said it all.

hunks.baseline: Then Han Yeop joined in, his voice wavering.
hunks.sol: Then Han Yeop cut in, his voice wavering.

hunks.baseline: “I-I don’t think that way.”
hunks.sol: “I-I don’t agree.”

hunks.baseline: “The Third Young Master—I mean Squad Leader—must have a reason for doing this… right?”
hunks.sol: “The Third Young Master—I mean, the Squad Leader—must have a reason for doing this… right?”

hunks.baseline: “What reason could there be? The Third Young Master spent his youth drinking with women instead of training. He caused every kind of trouble despite being like that. And that’s not all. He was also the one who caused this war—”
hunks.sol: “What reason could he possibly have? The Third Young Master spent his youth drinking with women instead of training. Even so, he went around causing every kind of trouble. And that’s not all. He was also the one who started this war—”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin flinched when I cut him off. He seemed to realize that he had made a mistake.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin flinched when I cut him off. He seemed to realize he had made a mistake.

hunks.baseline: “Wasn’t the Third Young Master the one who caused this war?”
hunks.sol: “Wasn’t the Third Young Master the one who started this war?”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin’s pride was too great for him to stop himself.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin’s pride was too great to let him stop there.

hunks.baseline: The words finally left his mouth, and a chilly silence descended.
hunks.sol: The moment the words left his mouth, an icy silence descended.

hunks.baseline: Someone’s throat bobbed loudly. Nine pairs of eyes turned toward Hyuk Mujin and me.
hunks.sol: Someone swallowed loudly. Nine pairs of eyes turned toward Hyuk Mujin and me.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, I slapped Hyuk Mujin across the cheek with my flat palm.
hunks.sol: At the same time, I slapped Hyuk Mujin across the face with my open palm.

hunks.baseline: His jaw twisted to the side. It was an ordinary slap, without even a trace of internal energy. His face was still dazed by the sudden turn of events when I struck him a second time.
hunks.sol: His head snapped to the side. It was an ordinary slap, without even a trace of internal energy. While he was still reeling from the sudden turn of events, I swung a second time.

hunks.baseline: He wasn’t completely helpless, at least. He raised his arm to block.
hunks.sol: He wasn’t completely helpless, at least. He raised an arm to block.

hunks.baseline: What he had failed to account for was the difference in strength.
hunks.sol: What he had failed to account for was the difference in our strength.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin’s upper body slammed into the ground. He sprang back up, a palm print stamped onto one cheek like a tattoo.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin’s upper body slammed into the ground. He sprang back up, my palm print stamped across one cheek like a tattoo.

hunks.baseline: He was properly furious now. As he charged at me with his eyes bulging, I hooked his leg and tripped him. At the same time, I put force into my left hand and struck him.
hunks.sol: Now he was properly pissed. He charged at me, eyes bulging, and I hooked his leg out from under him. At the same time, I put some strength into my left hand and struck him again.

hunks.baseline: His legs seemed to give out, and he staggered. After taking three consecutive blows with this much force, it was only natural that his head would be rattled.
hunks.sol: His legs nearly gave out, and he staggered. Three consecutive blows with that much force were bound to leave his skull rattling.

hunks.baseline: “What, were you saving your internal energy to boil soup?”
hunks.sol: “What, are you saving your internal energy to make soup with later?”

hunks.baseline: That got through to him. Strength filled his wavering legs, and power surged through his body. His eyes glared at me, venom dripping from them.
hunks.sol: That got through to him. His wavering legs steadied, and power surged through his body. His glare dripped venom.

hunks.baseline: “No, I won’t.”
hunks.sol: “I doubt it.”

hunks.baseline: I could see all of them. Compared to Lee Seogeun, he was far behind.
hunks.sol: I could see it all. Compared to Lee Seogeun, Hyuk Mujin was hopelessly outclassed.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin’s head snapped back. Sticky blood sprayed through the air in slow motion. His pupils were unfocused, and his legs hung limp.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin’s head snapped back. Thick blood sprayed through the air in slow motion. His pupils lost focus, and his legs went limp.
Yet somehow, he didn’t fall.

hunks.baseline: Yet somehow, he didn’t fall. He couldn’t—not unless I let go of his fist.
hunks.sol: He couldn’t—not unless I let go of his fist.

hunks.baseline: That was his limit. Hyuk Mujin could no longer endure and passed out. Something fell with a soft thud onto his body, sprawled out in a bizarre position.
hunks.sol: That was his limit. Hyuk Mujin finally passed out. As he lay sprawled in a bizarre position, something began pattering softly onto his body.

hunks.baseline: *An eye?*
hunks.sol: *Snow?*

hunks.baseline: I raised my head toward the sky. The winter sky was raining down small white scraps of garbage.
hunks.sol: I looked up. The winter sky was dumping tiny scraps of white garbage on us.

hunks.baseline: “Rest is over. We’re leaving.”
hunks.sol: “Break’s over. We’re leaving.”

hunks.baseline: I tossed out the words and turned away. Behind me, the reconnaissance squad members finally exhaled the breath they had been holding.
hunks.sol: I tossed out the words and turned away. Behind me, the reconnaissance squad members finally released the breaths they had been holding.

hunks.baseline: When Hyuk Mujin woke up two hours later, the first thing he did was charge at me.
hunks.sol: When Hyuk Mujin woke two hours later, the first thing he did was charge at me.

hunks.baseline: After another ringing slap, he passed out again. The other reconnaissance squad members dragged him into a corner of the cabin.
hunks.sol: Another satisfying slap knocked him out cold. The other reconnaissance squad members dragged him into a corner of the cabin.

hunks.baseline: According to one squad member who knew the surrounding area well, we should have reached Jeongyang before sunset at the latest.
hunks.sol: According to a squad member who knew the surrounding area well, we should have reached Jeongyang before sunset.

hunks.baseline: But there had been nothing we could do about the sudden blizzard, and this cabin was the only place we had managed to find.
hunks.sol: But there was nothing we could do about the sudden heavy snowfall, and this cabin was the only shelter we had managed to find.

hunks.baseline: Apparently, it was a hunter’s shelter known only to those familiar with the area.
hunks.sol: Apparently, it was a hunters’ shelter known only to people familiar with the area.

hunks.baseline: The mission might be delayed, but this was a hundred times better than walking through the snow all night, collapsing from exhaustion, and then running into the enemy.
hunks.sol: The mission might be delayed, but this was a hundred times better than trekking through the snow all night, running ourselves ragged, and then encountering the enemy.

hunks.baseline: It was Han Yeop. The squad members behind him glanced at me, gauging my reaction.
hunks.sol: It was Han Yeop. Behind him, the other squad members stole glances at me, trying to gauge my mood.

hunks.baseline: As I looked at the fidgeting reconnaissance squad members, a thought struck me.
hunks.sol: The sight of the fidgeting reconnaissance squad members gave me an idea.

hunks.baseline: Look at the vigorous nodding and those eyes full of passion.
hunks.sol: Look at those heads bobbing furiously. Look at those eyes burning with enthusiasm.

hunks.baseline: *Seeing is believing, my ass. One beating beats a hundred explanations.*
hunks.sol: *Forget seeing once. One beating beats hearing something a hundred times.*

hunks.baseline: One beating really was better than explaining a hundred times.
hunks.sol: One beating really was better than a hundred explanations.
It was around noon.

hunks.baseline: It was around noon. Sunlight flashed along a sword blade. That was all the martial artist saw.
hunks.sol: Sunlight flashed along a sword blade. That was the only thing the martial artist managed to see.

hunks.baseline: Blood poured from the gaping wound that stretched from his shoulder to his chest. It was a fatal injury. The martial artist knew he was going to die.
hunks.sol: Blood poured from the gaping wound that ran from his shoulder to his chest. There was no recovering from an injury like that. The martial artist knew he was going to die.

hunks.baseline: “The others… Please, let them live.”
hunks.sol: “The others… Please, spare them.”

hunks.baseline: His exhausted voice cut off abruptly. Looking at the martial artist’s wide-open eyes, a middle-aged man clicked his tongue.
hunks.sol: His fading voice cut off abruptly. A middle-aged man looked into the martial artist’s wide-open eyes and clicked his tongue.

hunks.baseline: “Good grief, you poor fool.”
What were you thinking, charging in like that?
hunks.sol: “Good grief, you poor fool. What were you thinking, charging in like that?”

hunks.baseline: The words that followed never reached the dead man. The fifty-odd wandering martial artists surrounding them snickered.
hunks.sol: The rest of his words never reached the dead man. The fifty-odd wandering martial artists surrounding them snickered.

hunks.baseline: “Only an orthodox-faction bastard would keep playing the hero right to the end. What should we do, Boss?”
hunks.sol: “Only an orthodox-faction bastard would keep playing the hero right to the bitter end. What should we do, Boss?”

hunks.baseline: Their gleaming eyes turned toward the survivors. There were six or seven women and children huddled together.
hunks.sol: Their gleaming eyes turned toward the remaining survivors—a group of six or seven women and children.

hunks.baseline: At the plea from the oldest-looking woman, the middle-aged man—Jopil, One Question, One Kill—smiled gently.
hunks.sol: At the plea from the oldest-looking woman, the middle-aged man—One Question, One Kill Jopil—smiled gently.

hunks.baseline: “I’m sorry, but what can I do? I’m no Great Hero.”
hunks.sol: “I’m sorry, but what can I say? I’m no Great Hero.”

hunks.baseline: “But you’re still a person. How can you kill children who can’t even tell right from wrong?”
hunks.sol: “But you’re still human. How can you kill children who can’t even tell right from wrong?”

hunks.baseline: “Hah. For a woman, you have quite a bit of spirit. Wait. I heard that the family of the Sakju Branch Leader survived. Could it be…?”
hunks.sol: “Hah. You have quite a bit of spirit for a woman. Wait. I heard the Sakju Branch Leader’s family survived. Could you be…?”

hunks.baseline: “Ah, so he is. I never imagined such a virtuous wife would belong to such a pathetic man.”
hunks.sol: “Ah, I thought so. Who would have imagined such a pathetic man could have such a virtuous wife?”

hunks.baseline: Jopil smiled broadly, and the woman’s expression hardened.
hunks.sol: Jopil smiled, and the woman’s expression hardened.

hunks.baseline: “Rest easy. I don’t have a taste for tormenting people.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t worry. I’m not in the habit of raping women before I kill them.”

hunks.baseline: “This is a harsh world. How are little ones supposed to survive without their mother?”
hunks.sol: “This is a harsh world. How could little ones survive without their mother?”

hunks.baseline: “I heard your last words.”
hunks.sol: “Last words duly noted.”

hunks.baseline: A short while later, the blood-soaked wandering martial artists tossed the corpses into the thickets in the mountains.
hunks.sol: A short while later, the blood-soaked wandering martial artists tossed the corpses into the mountain thickets.

hunks.baseline: “Only the wild animals will feast tonight.”
hunks.sol: “Looks like the wild animals will be the only ones feasting.”

hunks.baseline: The man with the tiny birdlike eyes muttered. He was Jopil’s right-hand man, a first-rate wandering martial artist known by the nickname Black Mountain Blade.
hunks.sol: The man with tiny, birdlike eyes muttered. He was Jopil’s right-hand man, a first-rate wandering martial artist known as Black Mountain Blade.

hunks.baseline: “We should feast, too. If we finish this job properly, what’s a mere thousand pieces of gold?”
hunks.sol: “We’ll feast too. If we finish this job properly, even a thousand pieces of gold will be within reach.”

hunks.baseline: Jopil laughed with pleasure. The payment for this job would be enormous, but the situation itself was what he enjoyed.
hunks.sol: Jopil laughed in delight. The payment for this job would be enormous, but he was enjoying the situation itself just as much.

hunks.baseline: His dirty leather shoe stepped on the fallen martial artist’s corpse.
hunks.sol: He planted a filthy leather shoe on the fallen martial artist’s corpse.

hunks.baseline: The martial artist had belonged to the Sakju Branch, one of the ten or so branches of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
hunks.sol: The dead man had belonged to the Sakju Branch, one of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s dozen or so branches.

hunks.baseline: “Was that the last one?”
hunks.sol: “Was that the last of them?”

hunks.baseline: “Three in total. One martial artist and two children. They passed through Jeongyang only a few hours ago and are headed for Honju.”
hunks.sol: “Three in total. One martial artist and two children. They passed through Jeongyang only a few hours ago and are heading for Honju.”

hunks.baseline: “You don’t need to go yourself. I’ll take care of it.”
hunks.sol: “There’s no need for you to go yourself, Boss. I’ll take care of it.”

hunks.baseline: “Would you?”
hunks.sol: “Will you?”

hunks.baseline: “Good. Take half of them with you. You have half a day. How does that sound?”
hunks.sol: “Good. Take half the men. You have half a day. How does that sound?”
There was only one possible answer.

hunks.baseline: Black Mountain Blade already knew the answer and bowed deeply.
hunks.sol: Black Mountain Blade bowed deeply.
